questions.question: Which built-in function is used to display output on the console in Python?
questions.explanation: print() is Python's built-in function for sending output to the console. echo is a shell/PHP command, console.log() is JavaScript, and System.out.println() is Java.

questions.question: Which symbol is used to start a single-line comment in Python?
questions.explanation: In Python, everything after # on a line is treated as a comment and ignored by the interpreter. // is a comment in C, C++ and Java, /* starts a block comment in those languages, and -- is a comment in SQL.

questions.question: What is the standard file extension for a Python source code file?
questions.explanation: Python source files use the .py extension, for example hello.py. The other extensions are not recognized as standard Python source files.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly prints Hello, World in Python 3?
questions.explanation: In Python 3, print is a function, so it must be called with parentheses: print("Hello, World"). The form without parentheses was valid only in Python 2. The other options belong to other languages.

questions.question: A file named hello.py is saved in the current folder. Which command runs it from the terminal?
questions.explanation: Running python followed by the script name executes the file. Python has no 'run' or '--execute' option for this. The -c option expects a string of Python code, not a file name, so python -c hello.py would try to run the text hello.py as code and fail.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

print("Hi", "there")
questions.explanation: print() accepts multiple arguments and joins them using the sep parameter, whose default value is a single space. So the output is Hi there. The tuple form appears only if you print a tuple object, not multiple arguments.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

print("A", "B", sep="-", end="!")
questions.explanation: sep="-" replaces the default space between the arguments, giving A-B. end="!" replaces the default newline at the end, so ! is printed right after B and the cursor stays on the same line. The result is A-B!.

questions.explanation: Python uses indentation to define blocks. After the if statement ends with a colon, the next line must be indented. Because print("Yes") is not indented, Python raises IndentationError: expected an indented block.

questions.question:
What happens when the following line is executed in Python 3?

Print("Hello")
options: It prints Hello along with a warning
questions.explanation: Python is case-sensitive. The built-in function is print in lowercase, and Print is a different, undefined name. The line is syntactically valid, so it fails at runtime with NameError: name 'Print' is not defined.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid way to continue a long Python statement onto the next line?
options: Put a backslash \ at the end of the line
Put a semicolon ; at the end of the line
Put three dots ... at the end of the line
Put a double slash // at the end of the line
questions.explanation: A backslash at the end of a line joins it with the next line (explicit line continuation). A statement can also continue across lines inside (), [] or {} without a backslash. A semicolon only separates statements, and ... and // do not continue a line.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

print(2 + 3, "2" + "3")
questions.explanation: 2 + 3 adds two integers and gives 5. "2" + "3" concatenates two strings and gives "23". print() then joins both values with a space, so the output is 5 23. No TypeError occurs because each + operates on matching types.

questions.question:
A file contains these two lines (the second line starts with two spaces):

print("Hello")
  print("World")

What is the result of running it?
options: Hello and World are printed on separate lines
Hello is printed, followed by an IndentationError
An IndentationError occurs and nothing is printed
HelloWorld is printed on one line
questions.explanation: Python reads and compiles the whole file before executing any of it. The unexpected indent on line 2 is detected during this parsing step, so IndentationError: unexpected indent is raised before the first print() ever runs. That is why even Hello is not printed.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

print(r"C:\new\table")
options: C:, then a line break, then ew, then a tab, then able
questions.explanation:
The r prefix makes this a raw string, so backslashes are treated as ordinary characters and escape sequences like 
 and 	 are not interpreted. The text is printed exactly as written: C:
ew	able. Without the r prefix, 
 would become a newline and 	 a tab.

questions.question: In a Python script, when does the code inside an `if __name__ == "__main__":` block run?
options: Only when the file is imported by another module
Every time the file is either imported or run
Only when Python is started in interactive mode
Only when the file is executed directly as the main script
questions.explanation: When a file is run directly, Python sets its __name__ variable to "__main__", so the block executes. When the file is imported, __name__ is set to the module's name instead, so the block is skipped. This lets a file work both as a runnable program and as a reusable module.

questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?

print("Hi", end="")
print("Bye", end="\n\n")
print("Done")
options: HiBye and Done on consecutive lines with no blank line
Hi, Bye and Done each on its own line
HiBye, then one blank line, then Done
Hi Bye, then Done on the next line
questions.explanation: The first print outputs Hi with no newline, so Bye continues on the same line, giving HiBye. The second print ends with two newline characters: the first ends the current line and the second produces an empty line. The last print then outputs Done on its own line.
